title: Freight Forwarding Manager (Sea & Air)
description: How would you like to build and lead the freight forwarding division of a logistics tech startup based in Ethiopia, starting with sea freight? How would you feel about being part of a Team that is on a mission to fix an incredibly inefficient logistics industry? (Apply Here: https://jobs.worksimplehr.com/jobs/garri-logistics-plc-1/logistics-manager-freight-forwarding-sea-air) What's The Job? As Freight Forwarding Manager, your task is to set up and run Garri's freight forwarding business from the ground up, with sea freight at its core: Build the division: services, processes, SOPs, pricing, and the team. Own sea freight imports and exports end to end (FCL, LCL, break bulk, RoRo, and project cargo): vessel booking, documentation, Djibouti port handling, transit, customs clearance, and final delivery. Run the Djibouti side of the operation: vessel arrivals, port and transit agents, free time, and getting cargo out of port fast. Choose the right import mode (multimodal or unimodal) for each shipment, and coordinate with Modjo and other dry ports. Build and manage relationships with shipping lines, NVOCCs, overseas agents, Djibouti transit agents, and clearing agents. Negotiate ocean freight rates and contracts, prepare competitive quotations, and protect the margin on every shipment. Grow air freight as a second service line, working with airlines and air cargo agents. Lead the licensing and regulatory setup for freight forwarding and customs clearance, and keep the division fully compliant. Win and grow customers (importers, exporters, manufacturers, and project cargo clients), including client meetings and tenders. Connect forwarding with Garri's trucking network and technology to offer true door-to-door service. Control costs and risks: demurrage, detention, storage, cargo insurance, claims, and the cash flow tied to freight and duties. Report volumes, revenue, margins, transit times, and customer satisfaction to management every month. Recruit, train, and lead the team, starting with an Ocean Freight Officer, and set clear targets for each person. Perform other duties assigned by the General Manager. Who Are We? Garri Logistics is a digital freight brokerage and fleet management platform in Ethiopia. We are building innovative tech products and services to bring a highly fragmented, low trust, and offline freight industry to an online marketplace while bringing much needed trust, quality, cost saving, and efficiency. Our goal is to make Garri Logistics the primary way to transport goods across Ethiopia. We are now adding sea and air freight forwarding, so our customers can move their cargo with one trusted partner, from the port of origin all the way to their door. What Skills Do You Need? 8+ years' experience in freight forwarding, including at least 5 years in sea freight operations and 3 years in a management role. Deep, hands-on sea freight expertise: FCL, LCL, break bulk, and project cargo, carrier bookings, bills of lading, and container management (free time, demurrage, detention). Strong knowledge of the Djibouti corridor, multimodal and unimodal imports, Ethiopian customs procedures, eSW, and dry port operations. Existing relationships with shipping lines, NVOCCs, overseas agents, Djibouti transit agents, and clearing agents. Solid understanding of Incoterms, letters of credit and bank documents, and cargo insurance. Proven record of winning customers and running a profitable forwarding operation or branch. Experience setting up a new division or office is a strong plus. Air freight experience (airline bookings, air waybills) is a plus. Comfortable with technology, and excited to help shape the software behind our forwarding business. Excellent leadership, organization, and entrepreneurial spirit (work under little or no guidance, and perform under pressure). Bachelor's degree in Logistics, Supply Chain Management, Maritime Studies, Business, or a related field. Excellent written and verbal English and Amharic skills. Compensation We offer competitive salary and benefits, and amazing opportunities to grow with us. What's In It For You? If you are looking for a rare chance to build a freight forwarding business from the ground up, backed by an established trucking network and our own technology, then this is a good fit. We are actively interviewing and looking to onboard quickly.

title: JPO - Strategic Planning and Analysis Analyst
description: Job Description IMPORTANT : This position is offered within the framework of the Junior Professional Officer (JPO) Programme and is open exclusively to nationals of Norway . Applicants must meet the eligibility requirements established for the JPO Programme and the specific requirements of the position. The UNDP Junior Professional Officer (JPO) Programme The UNDP (United Nations Development Programme) JPO Programme equips outstanding young leaders with the skills and experience required to advance the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and make a positive difference in the world. As a pathway into the world of development, the programme offers young professionals excellent exposure to multilateral cooperation and sustainable development while providing a valuable entry point into the UN system. During their assignments, JPOs benefit from the guidance of experienced UNDP staff members and are actively involved in supporting the design and implementation of UNDP’s programs within UNDP’s headquarters, regional or country offices. Additionally, the JPO will undergo a journey of exposure and growth which will build both personal and professional capacity for a career within the multilateral development sector. As a JPO and young professional in UNDP you should be interested in pursuing a global career with aspiration to work for a field-based organization in support of the development agenda. The JPO will work as part of a team and be supervised by an experienced UNDP staff member, including : Structured guidance and feedback, especially in the beginning of the assignment, with the purpose of gradually increasing of responsibilities Establishment of a work plan, with clear key results Guidance and advice in relation to learning and training opportunities within the field of expertise Completion of the yearly UNDP Annual Performance Review (APR) including learning and development objectives. The JPO will benefit from the following learning and development opportunities: Participation in a virtual Programme Policy and Operations Induction Course within the first 4 to 6 months of assignment Use of yearly JPO duty-related travel and training allocation (DTTA), as per the online DTTA guide On-going Masterclasses on relevant and inspiring themes Career development support mechanisms and activities Networking with fellow JPOs, young professionals and senior UNDP colleagues Mentoring programme Other training and learning opportunities Organisational context The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) is supporting the Government of Ethiopia in the implementation of the National Disarmament, Demobilization, and Reintegration Programme (NDRP) as part of broader efforts to consolidate peace and support recovery in conflict-affected regions. The NDRP is being implemented in diverse and politically sensitive settings, including Tigray, Oromia, Amhara, and other areas affected by conflict. These regions vary significantly in terms of their political dynamics, levels of insecurity, and the socio-economic realities faced by ex-combatants and host communities. In this context, the need for clear, consistent, and conflict-sensitive communication is paramount. The dissemination of DDR objectives and progress must be tailored to regional specificities while ensuring alignment with national narratives. Misinformation, political contestation, and diverging public expectations pose significant risks to the credibility and perceived neutrality of the DDR programme. As such, strategic communication and risk analysis are critical to mitigating tensions, building trust, and maintaining the programme’s momentum. This position is therefore essential to ensure UNDP’s work remains responsive to local realities, politically informed, and strategically positioned in Ethiopia’s complex recovery and peacebuilding landscape. UNDP’s DDR Unit in Ethiopia supports the nationally led stabilization and recovery process by coordinating development partner engagement and managing pooled funding in support of the National Demobilization and Reintegration Programme (NDRP), which is implemented by the National Rehabilitation Commission (NRC). The Unit’s key priorities include ensuring coherence among donor-supported initiatives, promoting conflict-sensitive programming, facilitating regional and federal-level coordination, and supporting monitoring, learning, and accountability frameworks. Given the diverse operational settings in which the NDRP is being implemented—including regions with different political dynamics, conflict legacies, and levels of community acceptance—the work of the DDR Unit is shaped by the need for careful messaging, timely political analysis, and strong collaboration with implementing and funding partners. This position is thus integral to ensuring that risk-informed, adaptive, and context-sensitive communication supports national DDR efforts and contributes to broader peacebuilding and stabilization outcomes. description: Who We Are Girl Effect is an international non-profit organization dedicated to addressing challenges faced by adolescent girls and youth in Ethiopia. Operating in the country since 2013, the organization leverages Social and Behavior Change (SBC) strategies, combining media and on-the-ground interventions to tackle various societal issues and empower young people. Girl Effect Ethiopia created the youth brand Yegna in 2014 and, since then, has reached over 10 million people through multiple products, outreach programs, girl networks, and research pieces done all for the betterment of adolescent lives. We arm girls with the skills to negotiate and redefine what they are told is possible, so every girl can choose to be in control of her body, her health, her learning and livelihood. When a girl unlocks her power to make different choices that change her life, it inspires others to do so too. She starts a ripple effect that impacts her family, community, and country. That’s the Girl Effect. Background Yegna Gize, meaning “Our Time” in Amharic, is a Girl Effect Ethiopia programme that builds on the Yegna brand and its experience of using media, storytelling, role modelling, and community engagement to influence positive social and behavioural change among young people. Yegna Gize focuses specifically on youth economic empowerment, with an emphasis on improving young people's aspirations, mindsets, skills, access to opportunities, and pathways towards employment and entrepreneurship. Over the programme period, Yegna Gize seeks to contribute to improved economic opportunities and livelihood outcomes for young people in Ethiopia by addressing barriers related to employment, entrepreneurship, skills development, social norms, and mindsets. The programme works with young people, schools, communities, government institutions, civil society organisations (CSOs), private-sector actors, role models, and other relevant stakeholders to create an enabling environment for youth to pursue viable economic pathways. The programme is implemented across six regions of Ethiopia: Tigray, Oromia, Amhara, Central Ethiopia, Sidama, and South Ethiopia. Through a combination of youth-centred interventions, partnerships, capacity strengthening, communication and social and behavioural change approaches, Yegna Gize aims to strengthen young people's knowledge, skills, confidence, aspirations, networks, and access to employment and entrepreneurship opportunities. Key areas of Yegna Gize programming include: Youth employment and transition to work: Supporting young people to access internships, work-based learning, employment opportunities, and other pathways into the labour market. Entrepreneurship and enterprise development: Strengthening entrepreneurial knowledge, business skills, growth mindsets, and access to support for young people interested in starting or growing businesses. Skills and mindset development: Building practical, transferable, entrepreneurial, and employability skills, alongside confidence, aspirations, resilience, and positive attitudes towards work and entrepreneurship. Peer-to-peer and youth support mechanisms: Establishing and strengthening youth groups and peer-support approaches that enable young people to learn from and support one another. Role modelling and mentorship: Connecting young people with role models, mentors, entrepreneurs, and other influential individuals who can provide inspiration, guidance, and practical exposure to different livelihood pathways. School-based engagement: Working with schools, teachers, students, and relevant stakeholders to promote entrepreneurship, creativity, growth mindset, career aspirations, and awareness of economic opportunities. Youth-centred media and social and behavioural change communication (SBC): Using Yegna's established multimedia and storytelling platforms to challenge limiting norms, promote positive attitudes towards work and entrepreneurship, and increase young people's awareness and uptake of available opportunities. Partnerships and systems strengthening: Working with regional and local government structures, CSOs, private-sector actors, educational institutions, and other stakeholders to strengthen the ecosystem supporting youth economic empowerment. Girl Effect works with local partners to contextualise and implement interventions according to regional realities and the needs of young people. The programme therefore combines national-level approaches with locally relevant implementation, allowing interventions to respond to the different economic, social, cultural, and institutional contexts across the six regions.
